stemMd: How should the0.1s differences among Experiment2’s ten-oscillation times be interpreted?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They prove the timer has no uncertainty.

options.label: B
options.textMd: They prove period doubles when mass doubles.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They establish exactly equal true periods for all masses.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They do not establish a mass effect because they are smaller than the stated reading uncertainty

explanationMd: The observed0.1s variation is smaller than a single interval’s0.2s reading uncertainty, so these measurements do not resolve a mass effect. This does not establish exact equality.

distractorRationale.c: Measurements with uncertainty cannot prove exact equality.
